The tide of the Ashwind Sea

The tide is semidiurnal: two high waters and two low waters in a tidal day of 24 h 50 min. Every high water arrives about fifty minutes later than the one on the day before.

Range

The tidal range is the height of high water minus the height of low water. At Torvig Harbour the mean range is 3.4 m, the spring range 5.1 m and the neap range 1.7 m — the spring range is exactly three times the neap range.

The rule of twelfths

Between low water and high water the water rises for six hours: one, two, three, three, two and one twelfth of the range. Half the range is reached after three hours, and the fastest rise falls in the third and fourth hour.

The Ovray rule

Ovray Cove dries out below 1.2 m above chart datum. Low water at springs is 0.3 m and at neaps 1.6 m, so the cove is unreachable at low water springs. Plan the arrival within two hours either side of high water.
